title: Measuring Generative AI Content in Political Campaigns: Evidence of Rising Adoption and Non-Disclosure
abstract: arXiv:2611.11658v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The use of generative AI in political campaigns has drawn public concern and policy attention. Public concerns range from distrust of candidates to skepticism about the authenticity and accuracy of political advertising, including AI-generated images and video. Nearly half of U.S. states have enacted laws that prohibit, or require disclosure of, "materially deceptive" AI-generated content (AIGC) in elections to guard against these concerns. This study measures how candidates and their campaigns produce and circulate AIGC during an election cycle. We develop two measures that estimate not only wether campaigns use AIGC, but how much they produce (magnitude) and in what forms (modality). We apply these measures to a novel dataset of text and images from the campaign websites, X accounts, and emails of 12,977 candidates for U.S. political office from 2023 to 2025. We report three findings. First, detectable AIGC from campaigns increased

translated_title: 测量政治竞选中的生成式AI内容：采用率上升与缺乏披露的证据
translated_abstract: 生成式AI在政治竞选中的使用引发了公众关注和政策重视。公众的担忧涵盖从对候选人的不信任，到对政治广告（包括AI生成的图像和视频）的真实性与准确性的怀疑。为防范这些担忧，美国近一半的州已颁布法律，禁止或要求披露选举中“具有实质性欺骗性”的AI生成内容（AIGC）。本研究测量了候选人及其竞选团队在一个选举周期内如何生产和传播AIGC。我们开发了两种测量方法，不仅可以估计竞选活动是否使用了AIGC，还能估计其产出的数量（规模）以及呈现的形式（模态）。我们将这些测量方法应用于一个新颖的数据集，其中包含2023年至2025年间12,977名美国政治职位候选人的竞选网站、X账号和电子邮件中的文本与图像。我们报告了三个发现。首先，可检测到的竞选活动产生的AIGC增加了……
tldr: 该研究开发了能够量化竞选活动中生成式AI内容使用规模与模态的新测量方法，基于对12,977名美国候选人网站、社交账号和邮件数据的分析，发现AI生成内容的使用正不断上升且普遍缺乏披露。
en_tdlr: This study develops novel measures to quantify both the magnitude and modality of generative AI content in political campaigns, and—using data from 12,977 U.S. candidates' websites, X accounts, and emails—provides evidence of rising AIGC adoption and widespread non-disclosure.
